name: Borexino
summary: Borexino performed real-time low-energy solar-neutrino spectroscopy in an exceptionally radiopure liquid-scintillator target at Gran Sasso. It measured components of the proton-proton chain and established the CNO-cycle neutrino signal, while also observing geoneutrinos.
detection_principle: Neutrino-electron elastic scattering produces scintillation light collected by photomultiplier tubes. Purification, a nested nylon containment system, a water muon veto and spectral analysis suppress and separate radioactive backgrounds; inverse beta decay identifies antineutrinos.

key_parameters.name: Scintillator
key_parameters.value: About 278 tonnes of organic liquid scintillator; analysis fiducial masses vary

key_parameters.name: CNO interaction rate
key_parameters.value: 6.7 +1.2/-0.8 counts per day per 100 tonnes in the final combined analysis

results.summary: The final CNO result combines spectral information with early Cherenkov-photon directionality and strengthens tests of the solar core composition.
Geoneutrino spectroscopy constrained terrestrial radiogenic heat and mantle contributions.
